sections.label: Bill repeals and amends legislation
sections.summary: The Bill repeals obsolete legislation, makes technical amendments, updates delegation of Ministerial functions and supports continuity of parliamentary sittings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Second, it repeals obsolete legislation and makes technical amendments to other Acts.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Third, it updates the framework for the delegation of Ministerial functions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Fourth, it supports the continuity arrangements for parliamentary sittings.

sections.label: Law Reform Commission revised edition
sections.summary: The Law Reform Commission is preparing a revised edition of the whole Statute Book.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Law Reform Commission is now in the midst of preparing a revised edition of the whole Statute Book.

sections.label: Authentic electronic Singapore Statute Book
sections.summary: The universal revision exercise supports AGC's move towards an authentic electronic Singapore Statute Book that is conclusive and replaces hard-copy text.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The universal revision exercise will support AGC’s move towards providing an authentic electronic Singapore Statute Book that is conclusive and in lieu of the hard-copy text.

sections.label: Repeal and re-enact section 36
sections.summary: Part 2 of the Bill repeals and re-enacts section 36 of the Interpretation Act to create a two-tier delegation framework.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To make this clear, Part 2 of the Bill repeals and re-enacts section 36 of the Interpretation Act to create a two-tier delegation framework.

sections.label: First tier statutory functions delegation
sections.summary: Almost all statutory functions can be delegated under the first tier.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Basically, almost all statutory functions can be delegated under this first tier.

sections.label: Second tier delegation to officers
sections.summary: Under the second tier, the responsible Minister may delegate functions to public officers and public bodies.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As for the second tier, the responsible Minister may delegate functions to public officers and public bodies.

sections.label: Smooth public administration and accountability
sections.summary: This passage states that delegation aims to ensure smooth, efficient public administration and timely services, while the responsible Minister remains accountable to Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This will help to ensure that public administration is carried out smoothly and efficiently to meet the challenges of the day and that services are delivered to the public in a timely fashion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: I should highlight that the responsible Minister remains accountable to Parliament for how a function is performed by his or her delegate.

sections.label: Definition of Parliament and communication links
sections.summary: Clause 14(a) amends the definition of Parliament to include any place appointed by the President, and Clause 14(b) makes it an offence to interfere with communication links between multiple sitting places.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clause 14(a) amends the definition of “Parliament” to include not just Parliament House, but also any other place that is appointed by the President.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Clause 14(b) of the Bill makes it an offence for a person to interfere with the communication links between the places where Parliament is sitting, should there be more than one place.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This is important as continuity arrangements are dependent on contemporaneous communication links, which allow Members to participate contemporaneously at a sitting from different locations.

sections.label: Delegation of Minister's function
sections.summary: The Bill proposes to allow delegation of a Minister's function to a public body or public officer unless contrary intention appears in the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the Bill proposes to allow the delegation of a Minister's function to a public body or public officer unless express or implied contrary intention appears in the Act.

sections.label: Factors for implied contrary intention
sections.summary: This passage asks the Minister to provide more specific guidance on factors to consider in inferring implied contrary intention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide more specific guidance on what factors should be considered in inferring implied contrary intention?

sections.label: Determining public body's state of mind
sections.summary: This passage asks the Minister to clarify how a public body's opinion, belief or state of mind should be determined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how a public body's opinion, belief or state of mind should be determined?

sections.label: Public agencies adopting Court's recommendation
sections.summary: This passage asks the Minister to share if there are plans for public agencies to adopt the Court's recommendation in practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share if there are plans for public agencies to adopt the Court’s recommendation in practice?

sections.label: Carltona devolution unaffected by section 36(8)
sections.summary: New section 36(8) of the Interpretation Act makes clear the Carltona devolution principle applied in Asia Development remains unaffected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The new section 36(8) of the Interpretation Act makes clear that the principle of the Carltona devolution, which has been applied by the Singapore Court of Appeal in Asia Development, remains unaffected.

sections.label: Phrase appears in many Acts
sections.summary: The phrase appears more than 70 times on the statute books, including in the Partnership, Medical Registration, Copyright and Companies Acts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In fact, this phrase appears more than 70 times on our statute books, and can be found in Acts such as the Partnership Act, Medical Registration Act, Copyright Act and Companies Act.

sections.label: Deciding intention against delegation
sections.summary: The exercise resembles deciding whether Carltona devolution applies, weighing factors like life, liberty, quasi-judicial nature and administrative volume.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The exercise is similar to deciding whether the common law doctrine of Carltona devolution, which I mentioned earlier, applies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, to illustrate, at one end of the spectrum, where a power affects life and liberty, or is quasi-judicial in nature, such as the hearing of an appeal, then unless the express language makes it clear, then it is likely that there is an intention against delegation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On the other end of the spectrum, where the function is administrative in nature and likely to involve a substantial volume, such as transmitting a document from one authority to another, then it is very unlikely that there would be an intention against delegation.

sections.label: Bill adopts Asia Development good practices
sections.summary: Established legal doctrines determine a public body's state of mind, and the administrative guidance adopts the good practices recommended in Asia Development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The broader point here though is that there are established legal doctrines which can be used to determine the state of mind of a public body, and this Bill does not seek to introduce anything which is fundamentally new or controverts existing principles in this regard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng's third question relates to good practices recommended by the Court of Appeal in Asia Development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The administrative guidance effectively adopts the good practices that were recommended by the Court of Appeal in Asia Development.
